name: Rofanplateau
kurzbeschreibung: The Rofan Plateau above Lake Achensee delights with the Rofanseilbahn cable car, the Airrofan skyglider, and scenic ridge hikes to Rofanspitze.
preis: Plateau freely accessible; Rofanseilbahn cable car chargeable (Achensee Erlebniscard valid)
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily mid-May to early November and mid-December to early April
beschreibung:
Overview

The sprawling and sun-drenched Rofan Plateau sits above 1,800 meters elevation in the heart of the Rofan mountains, creating a spectacular natural viewing balcony directly overlooking turquoise Lake Achensee. Flanked by the jagged limestone summits of the Hochiss (2,299 m), Rofanspitze, and Gschöllkopf, the high plateau presents a captivating landscape contrast: While sheer vertical rock faces drop dramatically to the north, the southern aspect unfolds into gently rolling alpine meadows dotted with alpine roses and mountain pines. Accessed via the Rofanseilbahn from Maurach, the plateau is a haven for families, hikers, and climbers. The sunny slopes support protected alpine flowers such as gentians and edelweiss, while on the Gschöllkopf peak, the 360-degree 'Adlerhorst' viewing platform perched like an eagle's nest provides breathtaking views across the Achen valley.

Route & Requirements

From the mountain station of the Rofanseilbahn at 1,840 meters, gentle gravel trails connect historic alpine huts such as the Mauritzalm and Erfurter Hütte in 10 to 15 minutes of easy walking. For enthusiastic mountain hikers, the plateau offers an extensive trail network: Popular ascents include the trek up the Hochiss – the highest peak in the Rofan – via secure mountain tracks (approx. 1.5 hours, difficulty T2 to T3) or the hike to the idyllic Zireiner See. Passionate climbers test their skills on the famous Achensee 5-Peaks Via Ferrata across five distinctive summits. Sturdy mountain boots with vibram soles and waterproof outerwear are essential in high-alpine limestone terrain.

Visit & Arrival

The Rofanseilbahn operates daily every fifteen minutes from mid-May until early November. The valley station in Maurach am Achensee features large car parks located directly along the B181 highway. Rail travelers arrive at Jenbach railway station and transfer directly to bus line 4080 heading straight to the Maurach Rofanseilbahn stop. The historic Achensee steam cog railway also runs to Maurach.

Tips

For an adrenaline thrill, experience the Airrofan Skyglider, soaring like an eagle at eighty kilometers per hour from the Gschöllkopf down into the bowl. Relax afterward with freshly baked Tyrolean Kaiserschmarrn on the sun deck of the Erfurter Hütte with panoramic views over sparkling Lake Achensee.
